memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor. So Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast. - Gen 4:4b-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice carefully what Scripture says. God looked with favour "on Abel and his offering" - the person first, then the gift. It was not merely the sheep versus the grain; it was the man behind the offering. Hebrews tells us Abel offered "by faith" (Heb 11:4). His worship flowed from a trusting heart, and God saw it.

Cain's response tells us much about his heart. Instead of humbling himself, he grew angry and downcast. When our worship is rejected, the honest question is not "Why did God do this to me?" but "What is God showing me about my heart?"

God is never fooled by outward religion. He sees past the offering to the one who offers it. This can feel uncomfortable, but it is actually grace - because God cares about us, not just our performance.

The same God who saw Abel's faith sees yours. And through Christ, your worship, however imperfect, is made acceptable to God (1 Pet 2:5). You do not have to earn His favour by a perfect offering; you receive it by faith in the perfect Offering, Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- When correction comes, do you respond with anger or humility?
- Is your worship flowing from real faith?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see my heart and not just my hands. Cleanse me from empty religion and give me the true faith that pleases You.
